record.original_question: When a non-reduced scheme X occurs as the eigenscheme of a tensor, what degrees can the irreducible components of X have, and which schemes can appear as such irreducible components?

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Let X be a non-reduced scheme which arises as eigenscheme of a tensor. What are the possible degrees of the irreducible components of X? And what are the schemes that can arise as irreducible components?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space of dimension $n+1$ and let $T \in \mathrm{Sym}^d(V^*) \otimes V$ (equivalently, a partially symmetric tensor, or a homogeneous polynomial map $\mathbb{C}^{n+1} \to \mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ of degree $d-1$ in each coordinate). An eigenvector of $T$ is a nonzero $v \in V$ such that $T(v,\ldots,v) = \lambda v$ for some scalar $\lambda$. The eigenscheme $X = X(T) \subset \mathbb{P}(V) = \mathbb{P}^n$ is the projective subscheme defined by the $2\times 2$ minors of the $(n+1)\times 2$ matrix whose columns are the coordinate vector and $T(v,\ldots,v)$; equivalently, the scheme cut out by the polynomials $v_i\, T(v,\ldots,v)_j - v_j\, T(v,\ldots,v)_i$ for all $i,j$.

Suppose the eigenscheme $X$ is non-reduced. Determine:

(a) the possible degrees that an irreducible component of $X$ may have;
(b) which projective subschemes of $\mathbb{P}^n$ can occur as an irreducible component of such a non-reduced eigenscheme $X$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about the structure of non-reduced eigenschemes of tensors. Web searches did not surface a published resolution classifying the possible degrees or schemes appearing as irreducible components of non-reduced eigenschemes. The problem appears to remain open.
